text_rules: Use 3-5 words max in Hinglish mixing Hindi keywords with English technical/money terms; always include a specific number (₹ price, GSM, or piece count) paired with a negative consequence word (CRACK, WASTE, बर्बाद) to create a curiosity gap that forces the tap.
layout: Place all hook text in the center 25%-70% vertical safe zone using large bold sans-serif font with black stroke; use product image or t-shirt close-up as the background with slight dark overlay so yellow (#FFD400) keyword text and white secondary text pop at thumbnail size on mobile.
patterns: Top-performing Indian business Reels thumbnails follow a 'specific loss + relatable mistake' formula — a rupee amount or piece count paired with a disaster word (CRACK, REJECT, SCAM) outperforms generic advice thumbnails by 5-10x. Winning covers use high-contrast yellow keyword on dark/product background with no face, keeping text brutally short so it reads instantly at 1-inch mobile preview size. The curiosity gap works best when viewers can't tell WHO made the mistake or HOW it happened without watching — question marks and Hindi words spike engagement because they feel personal to the Indian B2B buyer.
ig_patterns: High save-rate (1.7%+) Reels covers promise reusable diagnostic knowledge — '3 Checks', 'Feel Cheap? Check These' — using specific piece counts and GSM numbers that buyers bookmark as purchasing checklists. High share-rate (1.8%+) covers expose a common scam or mistake with a question format in Hindi ('लिखा...निकली?') that triggers 'my retailer friend needs to see this' impulse sharing. The winning formula for both saves AND shares is: ₹ loss amount or piece count + technical keyword (GSM, YARN, MOISTURE) + consequence word — all in under 5 words with yellow highlight on the money/technical term.
